main_body: A T-shaped timber post: a horizontal crossbeam (rows 9-17) on a long vertical pole (rows 18-47), seen largely face-on.
top_band: Crossbeam: orange rows 10-12 (3 rows, L=157) above a cream highlight row 13, then a darker front face rows 14-15. The pole has no top surface.
evidence: The crossbeam is a flat horizontal bar about 8 rows tall, with a 3-row lighter band, a cream stripe and a darker lower part. It reads more as a front-facing plank with banding than as a foreshortened top surface over a deep front face. The vertical pole beneath is a 2-3px straight shaft in pure elevation with no visible top and no base, so the post has no horizontal surface visible from above. The 3-row top is thin, the beam is only about as deep as a plank, and the support shows no 3/4 construction. This is a front elevation, so it fails.

style.evidence: The candidate has only 7 distinct colours against 38-40 in the references. Its median is 0 colours per full tile because the piece is under one tile wide. The pole is a flat 2-3px strip of one colour with a dark outline, with no grain or texture. The crossbeam has a few speckle dots but far less detail than the reference wood on the stall and well. The outline is a tinted brown, not neutral black, which is fine, but the shading is shallow and the density is much lower than the references.
